title: Canada announces $6 million in funding for UN humanitarian office
excerpt: The funding for the United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs will be distributed over three years.
bodyHtml:
The Government of Canada announced on November 3, 2026, that it is providing $6 million in funding to the United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA). This institutional support will be distributed over a three-year period to assist the organization in its efforts to provide humanitarian aid to people affected by conflict, disasters and displacement.

Secretary of State for International Development Randeep Sarai confirmed the funding during a meeting in Ottawa with Tom Fletcher, the United Nations Under-Secretary-General for Humanitarian Affairs and Emergency Relief Coordinator. The two officials discussed the global humanitarian landscape, including rising humanitarian needs and financial pressures on the international humanitarian system.

Canada is also contributing US$430 million toward urgent humanitarian needs identified in the 2026 Global Humanitarian Overview. Furthermore, Canada is scheduled to begin chairing the OCHA Donor Support Group in July 2027.
topic: Secretary of State Sarai reaffirms Canada’s support for United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs
